text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Skills Development Fund launches a new initiative to encourage corprations to develop Total Company Training Plans.
- Singapore Government to revise its economic growth forecast for this year and expects a weak fourth quarter.
- U.S. Boeing 707 cargo plane explodes over Ecuador, wreckage kills 100.
- Jakarta-listed PT Great Reiver International announces taking over local Disney licensee Ray Summers Pte Ltd, placed under judicial management in August.
- Indonesia's Sinar Mas Group, parent of Golden Amcol, clinches 30,234 sq ft residential plot for about Singapore $48 million.
- Recent turnaround in volatile electronics sector has attracted investor interest.
- Society of Remisiers (Singapore) asks Stock Exchange of Singapore for clearer guidelines on penalties for offences committed by remisiers.
- Global investment banks and securities houses are more optimistic about Singapore stock market.
- Strong re-rating of Sesdaq stocks helps boost market.
- Kian Ann Engineering announces it will launch initial public offer before end of month.
- Singapore Trade and Industry Minister Yeo Cheow Tong says growth in fourth quarter will be fairly weak.

- Singapore-based Asia Pulp and Paper Co in joint venture with Zhenjiang General Light Industry Corp, receives approval from China's State Council to set up 15.1 billion yuan paper mill in Zhenjiang in Jiangsu province.
- DBS Land takes 60 percent stake for Malaysian $5.85 million in Malaysian company Ipjora Holdings in its portfolio expansion into service apartments.
- Listed Pacific Century Regional Developments Ltd agrees to acquire 85 percent in 400-acre township development in Guangzhou.
- Listed conductor equipment maker Advanced Systems Automation share price soars 35 percent after re-rating of electronics sector.
